explanation: The catch block only logs the error and then falls through, so the function implicitly returns `undefined` after a failure. Callers have no way to distinguish 'fetch failed' from 'fetch succeeded with no data' — the error is swallowed instead of being rethrown or surfaced via a rejected promise, so failures propagate silently and can cause downstream code to misbehave on `undefined`.
